root_cause: The navigation controller's `navigate` function is called each time `autoComplete.start` renders a new results list. The original code used a closure variable `currentFocus` that persisted across renders because a guard flag (`_navListenerAttached`) prevented duplicate listeners but did not reset the focus index. When the list was re-filtered (e.g., after typing "l"), the stale `currentFocus` value caused ArrowDown to target an out-of-bounds index, and `update` set `aria-activedescendant` using the unclamped index before `addActive` clamped it.
repair_strategy: Store the focus index on the input field (`_currentFocus`) so it can be reset to -1 on every render. Update `update`, `addActive`, and `navigation` to read/write this shared property. Keep the `_navListenerAttached` guard to prevent duplicate keydown listeners. This ensures the focus index resets when the suggestion list changes, and `aria-activedescendant`/`aria-selected` always reflect the clamped index.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users will reliably move focus through suggestions with ArrowDown/ArrowUp, and pressing Enter will commit the currently highlighted suggestion. The `aria-selected` and `aria-activedescendant` attributes will always match the visible selection, even after the suggestion list is re-filtered.
functional_risks: If a custom `navigation` function is provided via `resultsList.navigation`, it will not receive the shared `_currentFocus` property and may behave differently.
The `_currentFocus` property persists on the input field across autoComplete instances if the same input is re-used; this is mitigated by resetting it on each `navigate` call.
verification_requirements: After typing "bl" then pressing ArrowDown once and Enter, the input value must be "Blackberry".
ArrowDown and ArrowUp should correctly wrap and update `aria-activedescendant` and `aria-selected` on the appropriate list item.
Escape should clear the input and close the suggestion list.
Tab should behave as an arrow down when the list is open and move focus away when closed.
Re-filtering the list (e.g., typing additional characters) resets the highlight to the first item.
